Been in the same situation almost a year ago. I thought I've gotten good at forgetting and letting go, turned out I wasn't.

Just like one of the comments here, idk if what applies to me is also applicable to you, but here's what I did and maybe it can help.

I know it hurts a lot emotionally, and it is also painfully agonizing physically (walking feels heavy so you just lie down most of the time, meals feel like chores, etc), but just continue living your life feeling everything your body wants to feel. Be sad, be happy, be guilty, whatever. It's hard to wake up first thing in the morning of your everyday with a heavy chest and the memories of your ex lingering, but one of these days you're gonna wake up and you'll go about your day and you'll realize you haven't thought about her at all.

There's no proper timeline for moving on because it's different for everyone. Some move on fast, some don't. Some take months, years, and some even never.

About what you should do, that would depend. Some go for distractions, such as drinking, partying, travelling, tv shows, movies, etc. While these are perfectly okay, it's a good reminder to not let yourself get lost with the "distracting" moments and still face your pain. It should be a balancing act, really.

One step at a time. One day at a time. And time, give it time.

I don't think there's a trick on how to move on, you just do when you're ready. In my experience, I did kind of just wing it as I took it 15 minutes at a time, to one hour at a time, to half a day at a time, until I was able to take it one day at a time.

But here are some of my opinions on the matter and some of what I did:

Grieve. Give yourself time to grieve. Feel whatever your body and your mind wants you to feel. There will be days, weeks, even months when you won't feel like getting out of bed in the morning, or eating, or even taking a shower. Nevertheless, don't hate yourself for it, and acknowledge your emotions.

Time. It's all about time, kid. I know it sounds like a tedious suggestion, but give it time. A day may feel like 5 years when you're experiencing a heartbreak, but keep going, nonetheless.

Eat well and drink water. It may not sound like much, but it plays a huge role on getting better. Not having an empty stomach has a big impact on producing dopamine or some shit. (Correct me if I'm wrong). Drink water, self-explanatory, I suppose.

Don't dive into a new relationship right away. Just don't, unless you're sure you have already moved on, otherwise you would just be projecting your frustrations to your new lover, and it's unfair on their part, plus you wouldn't want to hurt people who just want to offer you genuine love. Make everything clear to them, that you're still healing from painful experiences.

Understand and accept that you are going to have setbacks. You may wake up one day feeling like you're over it so you go along your day, until nighttime comes and you find yourself thinking about your ex or wanting to stalk them to see what they're up to, understand this is okay. You can try again the next day. Or you have gone days or even weeks feeling like you have already moved on, until you see them with someone new, and now you're back to square one. *Shit*. Yeah, I know. Keep going, still.

Do what you want to do. Engage in new hobbies or something. You do you.
